recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If Patient Administration still wants a preferred dentist or pharmacist extension beyond the existing patient-preferredPharmacy extension, handle that as a new FHIR Extension Pack proposal rather than a core Patient reconciliation change.
issue_request: FHIR-7963 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Administration issue asking that Patient.careProvider account for provider roles. The accepted disposition renamed the element to Patient.generalPractitioner, kept multiple cardinality, described it as the patient's gatekeeper or primary provider, and directed other role-based care providers to CareTeam and standard extensions.
initial_application: Git commit fb14d2fad17858e1b603cb0032db8a62b3563517 applied the source rename from Patient.careProvider to Patient.generalPractitioner, retained careProvider as an alias, updated examples/search parameters, and adjusted nearby Patient guidance. That commit also included unrelated Patient/RelatedPerson changes for FHIR-9366 and FHIR-3408.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively includes Patient, and source/patient/structuredefinition-Patient.xml now defines Patient.generalPractitioner as 0..* with careProvider as an alias, primary-care-provider wording, CareTeam role/history guidance, and Organization, Practitioner, and PractitionerRole targets. Later Jira decisions FHIR-14224 and FHIR-14442 added PractitionerRole and multiple-GP guidance, while FHIR-14734 confirmed generalPractitioner remains distinct from CareTeam. The FHIR Extension Pack currently contains patient-preferredPharmacy; no preferredDentist or preferredPharmacist definition was found in core or the extension pack.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current core source already preserves the approved semantic outcome: Patient.generalPractitioner is the active element, broad role/history use cases are directed to CareTeam, and later source history covers role disambiguation through PractitionerRole. Adding new core prose would be redundant, and creating any missing preferred dentist/pharmacist extension would be extension-pack work requiring fresh work-group review.
